Google Cloud suspended our production projects at 1am on Saturday, despite prior assurances everything was in order and billing was fixed.

Google Cloud is a weird thing: technically amazing (BigQuery, GKE) but half-assed as a product—console slower than AWS, support half-witted; even Alibaba Cloud didn't suspend my shit after a declined card.

Google has the worst support, bar none, of any infrastructure company I've dealt with in 13 years. You'll get better support for Google's own services from resellers who have on-call internal contacts.
A Google cloud service provider recommended storage changes to save money, which triggered a surprise $30,000 egress bill—this was the last straw that killed the company (Murfie).
A startup had prod pulled with no notice because their billing credit card was fraudulently used for Google Ad Words—same card used for GCP billing. Could happen to anyone.
As someone struggling with Google Cloud's mediocre support: we pay for support but tickets route through front-line staff with no context, isolating you from what's really going on during outages.

A keyword monitor picked up by Google's auto-moderation bot shut down our entire GCP project immediately; support said this would keep happening due to the 'grey area' of our tech and told us to move providers.
Typo'd a committed-use discount purchase on GCP, losing $5k in an unusable region; support said once clicked there's no undoing it, took days of escalation to fix.
We've been running ~400 servers on GCP for over a year and have been quite happy with performance, reliability, and support response when needed.
Persistent SSD requests started failing in us-west1-a for about a day; GCP support called the issue 'exceedingly rare' with no visibility or metrics, giving no clear timeline for resolution.

As a cloud provider I really like GCP compared to others—it's clean, consistent, predictable and easy to use. AWS always sent sales folks and Google always sent engineers, which makes me more comfortable.
GCP has been down since 11:50am and they acked it 35 mins later. They're great at leaving their customers in the dark.
GCP status page is worthless as it's always happy and green when production systems are down and then they might acknowledge something an hour later.
That feeling when you open console.cloud.google.com and see that you don't have your Kubernetes clusters and CloudSQL databases, but a CTA to create first.
Google Cloud is the number 4 most monitored status page on StatusGator; at least 20 other services we monitor seemingly depend on Google Cloud and posted issues as soon as Google went down.

GCP outage: the program that updates the Cloud Service Health status page is itself hosted on Google Cloud, delaying the incident report by about 1 hour because the status infrastructure was down too.
$ gcloud container clusters get-credentials returned ERROR: code=503, message=Visibility check was unavailable during a GCP outage—'we are truly in gods hands.'
The GCP outage page showed an orange 'One or more regions affected' marker while all services still displayed the green 'Available' marker, which apparently wasn't true.
